newsitem.title: USA: U.S. postal chief says no mail rate hike in 1997.
newsitem.headline: U.S. postal chief says no mail rate hike in 1997.

text.p: No price increase for mail is planned for the next year, the head of the U.S. Postal Service said Monday.

The last increase, to 32 cents from 29 cents for a domestic letter, was the only hike for four years and was less than the rate of inflation for the period, Postmaster General Marvin Runyon told the Anchorage Chamber of Commerce.
He said that the Postal Service had recorded several profitable years, and expected another one in 1997.
"So it will not be necessary to raise rates in 1997," he said.
Runyon was visiting Anchorage to mark the issuance of a new stamp commemorating the 100th anniversary of the Klondike gold rush.
